statement_summary: Derives stability/bifurcation conditions and analyzes order-dependent shifts of labelled Hopf threshold and chaos for one commensurate/incommensurate model.
proof_method: fractional characteristic equation + numerical bifurcation diagnostics
limitations: Does not supply a general incommensurate center-manifold/normal-form theorem; Hopf label must be read against finite-terminal periodicity semantics.
notes: Evidence of model-specific activity but not general closure.

assumptions: Specific double-Allee predation model and parameter regimes
statement_summary: Allee threshold/basin boundary may be a stable manifold of an equilibrium, a limit cycle, or a homoclinic orbit; separatrices reorganize through local/global bifurcations.
limitations: Integer-order/model-specific but very strong baseline; fractional work must exceed this geometry.

statement_summary: Any two one-dimensional solution trajectories either coincide or never intersect; higher-dimensional trajectories may meet.
limitations: Does not extend as nonintersection to general d>1 systems.
notes: Immediate scalar Allee threshold rigidity when compared with equilibrium trajectory x=a.

assumptions: Maximal-solution framework and source weak assumptions

limitations: Comparison theorem does not by itself classify multidimensional basin boundaries.

limitations: Requires monotonicity structure; does not make general multidimensional Caputo trajectories nonintersecting.

theorem_label: basin stability in infinite-dimensional delay state
assumptions: Initial histories in continuous-function space; choice of basis/sampling measure
statement_summary: Defines basin in function-space initial state and approximates basin volume by finite-dimensional basis expansion with cross-validation.
proof_method: history-space projection / Monte Carlo basin stability
limitations: Delay systems are not canonical Caputo, but state-space/basin-volume issue is directly analogous.
notes: Key methodological warning for physical-slice basin plots.

assumptions: Specific Double-Allee/group-defense model and sampled physical initial states
statement_summary: Computes probability of convergence to alternative stable states from sampled initial population densities; includes commensurate/incommensurate memory orders.
limitations: Does not characterize exact separatrix or full memory-state basin; sampling/horizon dependent.
notes: Strongest direct numerical prior against broad Double-Allee basin novelty.

assumptions: Positively invariant set separated from coordinate axes and source Lyapunov functional hypotheses
statement_summary: A Volterra-type logarithmic functional yields Mittag-Leffler stability on prescribed positively invariant subsets; extinction remains locally stable so coexistence is not globally attracting.
limitations: Not an exact basin characterization and does not identify the global separatrix.
notes: Classify as sufficient subset certificate, not basin theorem.

limitations: No general stable-manifold or full memory-state basin theorem identified.
